chain.label: Mountainous rising terrain along route (Muklung Hills)
chain.trigger: the accident site was to the east of the narrow pass between the Muklung Hills (the highest peak of which is depicted as 2,550 feet msl) and a smaller, unnamed peak

chain.label: Marginal VFR ceilings and variable low visibility along the route
chain.trigger: meteorological conditions that met the criteria for marginal visual flight rules were reported at Dillingham Airport... AIRMET Sierra for IFR conditions and mountain obscuration was issued at 1136 for the Bristol Bay zone

chain.label: Flight conducted low beneath cloud bases over rising terrain
chain.trigger: the airplane was at an altitude of about 1,080 feet msl at one point and... its next recorded altitudes were 780 feet msl and 920 feet msl

caused_by.evidence: Flight at such changing altitudes would be consistent with the pilot maneuvering to remain in VMC below the clouds and suggests the possibility of variable cloud ceilings along the flight route

chain.label: Pilot inhibited the TAWS aural voice and pop-up text terrain alerts
chain.trigger: the four bulb filaments for the “TERR INHB” annunciator were stretched (and two were broken)... therefore, the unit's visual alerts (and the GNS 530's voice and visual text pop-up TAWS alerts that it controlled) were inhibited

caused_by.evidence: the inhibit mode is provided because “flying [under VFR] into an area where unique terrain exists could cause the system to annunciate a nuisance alert”

chain.label: Reduced sleep opportunity, afternoon circadian low, and recent major life stressors
chain.trigger: the pilot had the opportunity to sleep a maximum of 9 hours on the night before the accident... which could represent up to 2 to 4 hours less overnight sleep than the pilot was accustomed to receiving... the accident occurred close to a time of day associated with lowered alertness (1500 to 1700)

chain.label: FAA issued unrestricted first-class medical certificate after the pilot's unexplained intracerebral hemorrhage
chain.trigger: the Alaska Regional Flight Surgeon's decision to issue the pilot an unrestricted first-class airman medical certificate, based largely on a local neurologist's in-office evaluation and without conferring with any other FAA physicians or consultants or attempting to address the etiology of the hemorrhage, the likelihood of recurrence, or the extent of any remaining cognitive deficit, was inappropriate

chain.label: Pilot's temporary unresponsiveness of undetermined origin
chain.trigger: the probable cause of this accident was the pilot's temporary unresponsiveness for reasons that could not be established from the available information

caused_by.evidence: although the pilot had some precursors for the development of fatigue, and the accident circumstances are consistent with fatigue impairment or a sleep event, there is insufficient evidence to determine whether fatigue-related performance or alertness impairments played a role

Because the pilot's previous ICH placed him at an elevated risk for subsequent cerebrovascular events... a medical condition leading to transient incapacitation or impairment could explain the circumstances of this accident

chain.label: Pilot unaware the airplane was approaching rising terrain
chain.trigger: the heading of the airplane at impact suggests that the pilot was largely unaware that the airplane was approaching the rising terrain

caused_by.evidence: This apparent lack of awareness suggests that the accident pilot's perceptions and/or responses became substantially impaired at some point after the airplane's last known Sky Connect position
had the pilot not inhibited the TAWS's aural voice and pop-up text alerts, the system would have provided an aural and visual alert up to 30 seconds before the impending collision

chain.label: Airplane tracked east-northeast into rising terrain instead of through the wide pass
chain.trigger: the airplane instead tracked to the east and collided with terrain about 4 nm southeast of its last recorded position... it was on a heading that pointed away from any relevant destination or previous flight track

caused_by.evidence: a deliberate execution of a left turn toward the rising terrain by the accident pilot in any weather condition would require a lack of situational awareness that is inconsistent with the pilot's reported level of proficiency
a turn to the right would overfly the low tundra... whereas a turn to the left would fly directly toward high terrain
the wreckage was found at an elevation of about 950 feet msl in steep, wooded terrain in the Muklung Hills

chain.label: Collision with mountainous, tree-covered terrain
chain.trigger: impacted mountainous, tree-covered terrain about 10 nautical miles northeast of Aleknagik, Alaska

caused_by.evidence: the airplane was in a climbing left turn when it collided with terrain and that flight control inputs occurred shortly before terrain impact

chain.label: Five fatalities and four serious injuries
chain.trigger: The airline transport pilot and four passengers received fatal injuries, and four passengers received serious injuries

caused_by.evidence: The cause of death for the pilot was listed as “multiple blunt force injuries of the head, neck, trunk, and extremities”
